title: Bardstown
summary: Bardstown, among Kentucky's oldest towns, began in 1780 when William Bard platted a town on a 1,000-acre land grant, first calling it Salem.
bodyMarkdown:
Bardstown is among the oldest towns in Kentucky: frontiersmen explored the area in the mid-1770s, and permanent settlement followed in 1780. This was a [time when](https://grokipedia.com/page/Bardstown,_Kentucky) Native nations were actively resisting settler encroachment.

## The Bard grant

That year William Bard arrived as agent for his brother David Bard and partner John C. Owings. He surveyed and platted a town on their 1,000-acre land grant. The settlement was first called Salem but was soon renamed for the Bard family.

The sources differ on the early dates. Another account of [Bardstown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bardstown,_Kentucky) gives 1780 as the settlement date but its wording places Salem's start a year later. One account dates the town's formal incorporation to 1788, while another lists incorporation in 1790. Both call Bardstown one of Kentucky's oldest towns, and one ranks it second-oldest, a ranking the other does not repeat.

## County seat on the Beech Fork

Bardstown became the seat of the new Nelson County in 1784. The county was [carved](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nelson_County,_Kentucky) from Jefferson County and named for Thomas Nelson Jr., a Virginia governor and signer of the Declaration of Independence. That entry gives two different creation dates, October 18 and December 5, 1784.

Migrants came mainly from Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania in search of farmland along the Beech Fork of the Salt River. A wave of Catholic families from Maryland arrived around 1785 and settled along the streams of the county.

## A Catholic center in the West

Those Catholic settlers made Bardstown a religious capital. On February 8, 1808, the Diocese of Bardstown was created to serve Catholics between the Appalachians and the Mississippi River. Benedict Joseph Flaget, a French Sulpician priest, became its first bishop and arrived in Bardstown in June 1811.

The Basilica of St. Joseph Proto-Cathedral was built between 1816 and 1819. It is [described as the first Catholic cathedral](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nelson_County,_Kentucky) west of the Allegheny Mountains.

## Slavery in Nelson County

Slavery underpinned both farming and institutions in and around Bardstown. In 1850 Nelson County [had 1,053 slaveholders](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nelson_County,_Kentucky). They held 4,918 enslaved Black people and 578 enslaved people described in census terms as mixed race.

## Kentucky today

Bardstown remains the Nelson County seat. Known since the 1950s as the Bourbon Capital of the World, it is a center of the Kentucky Bourbon Trail. Federal Hill, at My Old Kentucky Home State Park, and the proto-cathedral draw visitors to the historic town.
